title: Resource Allocation with Midterm Review
abstract: arXiv:2610.15786v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A principal funds an agent's project over two periods, with a midterm review providing a public signal about project quality. The agent privately knows the project's quality and always prefers more funding, while the principal wants to match funding to quality. We show that the optimal mechanism frontloads the review's information value: the principal's expected payoff is strictly higher in the first period than in the second, even though she is better informed after the review. In the optimal mechanism, higher-quality projects receive more funding initially but face larger cuts after a bad review, leaving them with less funding than lower-quality projects. A good review increases funding, but the resulting allocation does not preserve the initial ranking of projects and, under a mild condition, declines with quality near the top.

translated_title: 带有中期评估的资源分配
translated_abstract: 委托人在两个时期为代理人的项目提供资金，其中期评估会提供关于项目质量的公开信号。代理人私下知晓项目的质量，且总是偏好获得更多资金，而委托人则希望资金与项目质量相匹配。我们证明，最优机制会将评估的信息价值前置：即使委托人在评估之后掌握更多信息，她在第一时期的期望收益也严格高于第二时期。在最优机制下，质量较高的项目最初获得更多资金，但在不利的评估之后面临更大的削减，最终其获得的资金反而少于质量较低的项目。有利的评估会增加资金，但由此产生的资金配置并不保留项目的初始排序，并且在温和的条件下，资金在质量接近最高端时随质量上升而下降。
tldr: 最优资助机制会将中期评估的信息价值前置：高质量项目起初获得更多资金，但在不利评估后削减幅度更大，最终资金反而少于低质量项目，且良好评估后的资金配置可能颠覆项目的初始排序。
en_tdlr: The optimal funding mechanism frontloads the midterm review's information value: higher-quality projects receive more initial funding but face larger cuts after bad reviews, ending up with less funding than lower-quality ones, and good reviews can overturn the initial ranking of projects.
